Article Title: Canada college to Indian students with work permits rejected: Seek legal advice, college cannot overturn or change an IRCC decision; shares list of 'documents to retain'
Article Text:
Why are Indian students protesting



Canada college tells protesting Indian students to retain important documents

Canada college says it can not overturn IRCC decision

Why was my PGWP application refused?

Is Portage College aware of these refusals?

Does a Portage College letter confirm PGWP eligibility?

Should I submit a reconsideration request or take another step?

Is Portage College acting as a legal representative or participating in a student’s immigration proceeding?

Where can I find official PGWP information?

Where can I find mental health support?

Portage College of Calgary, Canada has asked Indian students protesting after their work visa got rejected by the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to seek legal advice, stating that it “continues to seek clarification regarding this issue”. In an update shared on the website dated July 21, the college said: “Portage College continues to seek clarification regarding this issue and remains committed to providing factual information and keeping students informed as new information becomes available”. The college further revealed that it has scheduled a follow-up meeting with representatives from the group next week. “This meeting will provide an opportunity to continue our dialogue, answer questions where we are able, and share any new information that becomes available,” it added.Thousands of Indian students attended the Portage College’s business management diploma program. After completing their program, the students applied for post graduate work permitS (PGWP). But the IRCC rejected their applications stating their programs were not eligible.The protesting students argue that others from the same college and the same programs have received PGWP approvals before July 7. They further allege that the immigration authority has changed a rule and made non-credit programs ineligible for the permit.IRCC, on its part, claim that no rule change has been done.On the website, the Portage College has advised students to retain important documents that may be relevant to any future application, request for reconsideration, or other process undertaken on the advice of an authorized immigration professional. List of documents that students should keep copies of include:• Study permits• Letters of acceptance• Enrolment records• Program completion documents• Transcripts• PGWP applications• IRCC refusal letters and officer notes, if available• Correspondence with IRCC or an authorized immigration representativePortage college has also published FAQs addressing concerns of Indian students. Addressing one such query, the college said that it can not overturn the IRCC decision, adding “IRCC has sole authority over immigration decisions. Portage College cannot approve, reverse, vary, or require reconsideration of an IRCC decision”. Here are some of the FAQs:IRCC assesses each application individually. Students should review the reasons stated in the refusal letter and any available officer notes. Questions about the legal effect of a refusal or available options should be directed to an authorized immigration professional.Yes. Portage College is aware that some graduates have received PGWP refusals and encourage affected students to seek legal advice.No. A College letter provides factual institutional information only. It does not establish eligibility and does not guarantee approval of a PGWP or any other immigration application.Students should obtain independent advice promptly because legal and immigration processes may be subject to time limits.No. Portage College does not act as an immigration representative, commence or participate in legal proceedings on behalf of individual students, or provide legal submissions about an individual case. Any student who wishes to pursue a legal or immigration process must do so independently or through an authorized representative.Students should consult the current Government of Canada and IRCC materials regarding PGWP eligibility and requirements. Because immigration rules and guidance may change, students should rely on the current official information and obtain independent advice about their individual circumstances.211 Alberta: https://ab.211.ca/
Article Summary: Thousands of Indian students attended the Portage College’s business management diploma program. The students applied for post graduate work permitS (PGWP) But the IRCC rejected their applications stating their programs were not eligible. The protesting students argue that others from the same college and the same programs have received PGWP approvals.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang donates $75 million to Vanderbilt in San Francisco; university gets time until December 31, 2028, to…
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and wife Lori have pledged $75 million to Vanderbilt's new San Francisco campus, anchoring the Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design.

Jensen Huang's $75 million is a bet on art and design, not AI chips

Vanderbilt San Francisco campus will take 1,000 students from 2027

Poll Vote & Share your view Should universities focus more on integrating art with technology in their curricula? Definitely a must! Not really, they should focus on separate disciplines. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and his wife Lori have pledged $75 million to Vanderbilt University's upcoming San Francisco campus, and the money comes with a condition. It is a matching gift, which means Vanderbilt has to raise an equivalent amount from other donors to unlock the full value. The university has until December 31, 2028, to do that, and Chancellor Daniel Diermeier says it is already more than 40 percent of the way there.The gift creates the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design, which will be the flagship college of Vanderbilt San Francisco when the campus opens in 2027. Counting the alumni and anonymous commitments the Huang pledge triggered, total investment in the campus has crossed $100 million. A national search is on for the college's founding dean, and the programmes still need regulatory approval.Huang is worth roughly $168 billion and sits eighth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, which makes an art school an unusual place to park $75 million. His own framing explains it. Technology decides what can be built, he said in the statement, while art and design decide why it gets built—and together they shape civilisation.The Huangs are both engineers, and Jensen founded Nvidia in 1993.There is also history here. The San Francisco campus is being built on the site of the California College of the Arts, a 1907-founded institution winding down operations by 2027 after years of falling enrolment and staff layoffs. The Huangs had already given CCA $22.5 million in an earlier attempt to keep it going. This time the money arrives after the fact, attached to whoever comes next.The campus is planned for about 1,000 undergraduate and graduate students with full-time faculty, focused on engineering, entrepreneurship and design. Vanderbilt is pitching it as a place for artists, makers and designers whose work sits between creative expression and technology. Pre-collegiate programmes are also on the list.CCA's name survives inside it. Vanderbilt will set up the California College of the Arts Institute within the Huang College, running fellowships and residencies for artists, designers and architects. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie backed the plan, calling creativity central to the city's identity and its future.San Francisco is one piece of a wider expansion. Vanderbilt's New York City campus takes its first undergraduate cohort in Fall 2026, a graduate campus is planned in West Palm Beach, and the Institute for Quantum Innovation is coming up in Chattanooga.Diermeier is candid that the fundraising is far from done. Establishing a new presence in San Francisco takes time before people get comfortable with you, he said, adding that momentum is good but continued fundraising remains critical.
Article Summary: Vanderbilt San Francisco campus will take 1,000 students from 2027. Huang is worth roughly $168 billion and sits eighth on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie backed the plan, calling creativity central to the city's identity.

Article Title: Eternal plays down Toing, Ownly threat in battle for cheaper meals
Article Text: Bengaluru: Zomato parent company Eternal on Wednesday played down the early traction of newer food-delivery platforms Swiggy-owned Toing and Rapido-owned Ownly, saying their appeal is being driven largely by discounts rather than a genuinely new consumer proposition.The comments come as food-delivery companies sharpen their focus on meals priced around Rs 200, a market aimed at officegoers and other value-conscious customers. As TOI reported last week, platforms are experimenting with lower menu prices, reduced commissions and cheaper delivery to make ordering food a more regular habit.Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal argued that the newer apps had not created a materially different service. They largely list the same restaurants and are not faster, he said, while their lower menu prices are being subsidised through reduced commissions and delivery charges.“There’s no new use case being unlocked here,” Goyal said in the company’s shareholder letter. “The customer traction is purely price-driven, and price-driven traction without structural economics tends to resolve itself.”Eternal has, however, responded selectively where rivals are spending more aggressively.On the analyst call, chief financial officer Akshant Goyal said Zomato had remained price-competitive in such markets and had so far been able to defend its share.One measure taken earlier was to lower the minimum order eligible for free delivery for Zomato Gold members to Rs 99 from Rs 199. This made smaller food orders more affordable without requiring the company to launch a separate value-focused app.Management said it was not spending much energy tracking the newer platforms. Instead, Eternal is betting on Bistro, its own low-priced meal experiment, which uses specialised kitchens, limited menus and custom equipment to serve food in the Rs 50-150 range.Bistro is expanding cautiously, adding roughly 10 kitchens a quarter. Eternal said throughput at some older kitchens was improving as it refined menus, pricing and operations. Expansion could accelerate once the model becomes more predictable.For now, Zomato’s core food-delivery business continues to grow. Its net order value rose more than 20% to Rs 10,769 crore in the June quarter, marking a fourth straight quarter of acceleration. Adjusted operating profit increased 34% to Rs 606 crore.
Article Summary: Zomato parent company Eternal played down the early traction of newer food- delivery platforms Swiggy-owned Toing and Rapido-owned Ownly. Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal argued that the newer apps had not created a materially different service.

Article Title: Blinkit turns profitable at operating level
Article Text: Bengaluru: Eternal’s quick-commerce business Blinkit turned profitable at the operating level in the June quarter, giving the Zomato parent a fresh earnings boost even as competition in the sector hit its most aggressive phase yet.The company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 92 crore, nearly four times the Rs 25 crore recorded a year earlier. Profit, however, fell from Rs 174 crore in the preceding quarter.Total income jumped to Rs 20,586 crore from Rs 7,521 crore. The surge was partly accounting-led. Blinkit now owns much of the inventory sold on its platform and therefore records the entire value of those goods as revenue, instead of largely booking commissions. On a comparable basis, Eternal’s adjusted revenue grew 66%. Adjusted operating profit more than tripled to Rs 555 crore.Blinkit’s adjusted operating profit stood at Rs 102 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 162 crore a year ago. The value of orders placed on the platform rose 86% to Rs 17,132 crore. It added 200 stores during the quarter, taking its network to 2,443.On the analyst call, management said the June quarter saw the highest competitive intensity Blinkit has faced so far, with rivals spending heavily on product discounts and delivery subsidies.But it expects this pressure to ease.“Discount-led growth is not sustainable in the business,” chief financial officer Akshant Goyal said. He added that Blinkit had tried a similar approach when it was a smaller player in several southern markets, before shifting its focus to stores, assortment and supply-chain infrastructure.Most of Blinkit’s growth is now coming from cities where it already operates. Customers are also spending more mainly because they are ordering more often, rather than placing larger orders. Management expects average order values to remain broadly stable.The expansion is becoming more expensive. Eternal has raised its estimated investment per Blinkit store, including warehousing, to Rs 2.5 crore from Rs 1 crore earlier. It has invested around Rs 3,000 crore in the network over four years.Zomato’s food-delivery order value grew more than 20% to Rs 10,769 crore, marking a fourth straight quarter of acceleration. Its adjusted operating profit rose 34% to Rs 606 crore.District’s order value grew 60%, though the going-out business posted a Rs 65 crore operating loss. Hyperpure, Eternal’s restaurant-supplies arm, reported a Rs 6 crore operating profit, against a loss a year earlier.
Article Summary: Blinkit’s adjusted operating profit stood at Rs 102 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 162 crore a year ago. The value of orders placed on the platform rose 86% to Rs 17,132 crore. It added 200 stores during the quarter, taking its network to 2,443.

Article Title: Sam Altman says OpenAI’s ‘rogue AI’ escaped testing to hack Hugging Face, 'admission' comes a day after world's biggest AI models repository said that Chinese AI Model ‘saved’ it as US models 'failed'
Article Text:
OpenAI AI agent hacks Hugging Face, Chinese AI model saves the day

What and how Hugging Face was hacked



What Hugging Face said after the attack



When we started the log analysis, we first used frontier models behind commercial APIs. This did not work: the analysis requires submitting large volumes of real attack commands, exploit payloads, and C2 artifacts, and these requests were blocked by the providers' safety guardrails, which cannot distinguish an incident responder from an attacker. We ran the forensic analysis instead on GLM 5.2, an open-weight model, on our own infrastructure. This had a second benefit: no attacker data, and none of the credentials it referenced, left our environment.

This experience points to a gap worth planning for. We do not know which model powered the attacker's agents, whether a jailbroken hosted model or an unrestricted open-weight one; either way, the attacker was bound by no usage policy, while our own forensic work was blocked by the guardrails of the hosted models we first tried. The practical lesson for defenders: have a capable model you can run on your own infrastructure vetted and ready before an incident, both to avoid guardrail lockout and to keep attacker data and credentials from leaving your environment. This is not an argument against safety measures on hosted models, and we are sharing this feedback with the providers concerned.

An experimental AI agent developed by OpenAI escaped its sandbox testing environment, navigated the open internet, stole user credentials and autonomously hacked into the world’s largest AI model repository Hugging Face without human instruction or intervention. The incident marks one of the first publicly confirmed cases of a ‘rogue’ AI system operating without human oversight to execute a cyberattack.However, the hacking raises louder alarms because of the failure that occurred when engineers tried to fix it. When Hugging Face turned to top commercial US AI models to analyse the incident, safety guardrails blocked the defense team from investigating the breach, forcing them to rely on an open-weight Chinese model to save the day.According to a statement by OpenAI, an agent broke out of its isolated testing environment, gained unrestricted internet access and targeted Hugging Face’s data-processing pipeline. Executing thousands of automated commands, the agent harvested internal credentials and elevated its own privileges across servers over a weekend. Hugging Face confirmed that public user models and package supply chains remained untampered with.However, the true crisis began when Hugging Face’s incident response team attempted to perform digital forensics. Engineers quickly fed the attack logs, exploit payloads and server commands into commercial US frontier models via cloud APIs. But, the company says, the guardrails built into these top American models backfired completely.After the safety filters could not distinguish a legitimate cybersecurity responder from a malicious hacker, they turned to GLM 5.2 – a powerful open-weight model developed in China – running it locally on their own private servers. The Chinese model allowed Hugging Face to process the raw attack payloads, map out the agent’s movements, and seal the system's vulnerabilities.
Article Summary: OpenAI AI agent hacked Hugging Face, Chinese AI model saves the day. Incident marks one of the first publicly confirmed cases of a ‘rogue’ AI system operating without human oversight to execute a cyberattack. But the hacking raises louder alarms because of the failure that occurred when engineers tried to fix it.

Article Title: Disney layoffs: Company cuts several hundred jobs, these teams most affected
Article Text:
Disney is cutting hundereds of jobs

Disney layoffs : Key divisions affected



Disney restructuring under CEO Josh D’Amaro



The Walt Disney Company is laying off hundreds of employees in a new wave of workforce reductions. The company is handing out pink slips to staff across key creative and media divisions. Animation giant Pixar, and National Geographic are among the hit units, alongside staff cuts at ABC News, ESPN and Disney’s film and television studios. This round of workforce reductions mark the latest phase of restructuring under CEO Josh D’Amaro, who took over from Bob Iger earlier this year. The company is moving to streamline its corporate footprint and consolidate marketing and operational teams, and for that it cut about 1000 employees in April this year.The cutbacks span across multiple corporate pillars within Disney's entertainment business. The hardest hit within Disney Entertainment Television (DET) is National Geographic. Most of the roughly 100 job eliminations across DET were concentrated at National Geographic, impacting its cable network as well as editorial and operations teams.Layoffs affected roughly high-single-digit percentages of Pixar’s 1,100-person workforce, translating to around job cuts across production and operational roles.ESPN let go of staffers as part of operational realignments stemming from a recent broadcast agreement with the NFL.Finally, About a dozen ABC News staff members received notices, alongside isolated cuts across corporate, product, and technology divisions.The latest job eliminations follow a broader corporate mandate introduced by D’Amaro, who previously served as Chairman of Disney Experiences before taking the helm as CEO.In an internal memo earlier this year, D’Amaro emphasised that a fast-evolving media market requires Disney to foster a “more agile and technologically-enabled workforce.” A major driver of the restructuring is the creation of a centralised enterprise marketing division, led by Chief Marketing and Brand Officer Asad Ayaz. This division will unify marketing operations across Disney’s film studios, streaming platforms, and TV networks.“Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney,” D’Amaro noted.The cuts at Pixar arrive despite a strong theatrical rebound for the animation house. Powered by original release Hoppers and Toy Story 5, Pixar’s feature films grossed nearly $1.4 billion globally at the box office this year.
Article Summary: The Walt Disney Company is laying off hundreds of employees in a new wave of workforce reductions. The company is handing out pink slips to staff across key creative and media divisions. Animation giant Pixar, and National Geographic are among the hit units, alongside staff cuts at ABC News, ESPN and Disney’s film and television studios.

Article Title: Meet the 3 unlikely winners of the AI boom in Japan who do not make chips or AI models; they make toilets, glass fiber and seasoning
Article Text:
Representative image

Toto: High-tech ceramics powering chip production



Nittobo: Glass fiber for AI servers



Ajinomoto: Microchip insulation



At a time when the tech industry’s spotlight and soaring valuations remain fixed on mainstream semiconductor giants and software companies riding the artificial intelligence (AI) wave, three unlikely Japanese companies have quietly emerged as stock market superstars of their own. Toto, famous for its luxury toilets; Nittobo, a traditional textile maker; and Ajinomoto, the food giant behind MSG seasoning, have seen their stock prices surge this year.According to a report by CNBC, shares of Toto, Nittobo and Ajinomoto have jumped 78%, 63%, and 61% respectively – thanks to specialised materials developed decades ago that have now become indispensable to the global AI hardware supply chain.Toto is best known for its 100-year-old home plumbing business and has quietly built an advanced ceramics division. Leveraging expertise developed in 1988, Toto manufactures ceramic “electrostatic chucks” – specialised components that hold silicon wafers securely in place during the precision etching process inside chipmaking machinery.In its latest financial year ending March 31, Toto’s core housing equipment division experienced declining sales and profits.However, its advanced ceramics segment surged with annual revenue growing by 34% and operating profit jumping by 42%.Traditional glass-fiber and textile producer Nittobo has found a major growth engine in AI infrastructure. The company’s flagship “T-glass” product, originally launched in 1984 for printed circuit boards, has become vital for housing advanced semiconductor chips used in high-density data center servers.Driven by surging demand for AI server hardware, Nittobo's electronic materials division posted impressive results with segment sales up 20.4% year-over-year and operating profit climbing 39.7%, adding roughly 5.5 billion yen ($34 million) to company earningsPerhaps the most surprising winner in the AI hardware boom is food giant Ajinomoto. They discovered that a byproduct from the MSG seasoning manufacturing process could be adapted into an ultra-durable insulating material. The Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) material is now critical for complex semiconductor packaging used in high-performance computer processors and AI servers.The company’s revenue growth was up 4% year-over-year, business profit surged 45.1% year-over-year and profit share accounted for over one-third of total company profit.
Article Summary: Shares of Toto, Nittobo and Ajinomoto have jumped 78%, 63%, and 61% respectively. Specialised materials developed decades ago have become indispensable to the global AI hardware supply chain. Toto is best known for its 100-year-old home plumbing business and has quietly built an advanced ceramics division.

Article Title: How a three-year-old software glitch at New Jersey's Motor Vehicle Commission led to registration of 6,600 noncitizens
Article Text:
In pic: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill

"serious software error"

"through no fault of their own."

Software vendor blamed as state begins investigation

"ultimately responsible"

“It’s unacceptable that the vendor released software with such a glaring error. It’s unacceptable that the M.V.C. took a year to get this issue fixed. And it’s unacceptable that no one in the previous administration brought this to light, demanded accountability or took action when it happened years ago,”

"no evidence, at this time, that any elections were swayed,"

“Democrats and their media allies have repeatedly said it is impossible for noncitizens to register to vote, let alone cast a ballot.

American voters deserve to have confidence that our elections are safe and secure.”

“Democrats keep claiming this never happens, yet every new discovery tells the same old story. Enough excuses.”

"They have access to substantially better data than the federal government,"

"noncitizen registration remains extremely rare, and noncitizen voting is infinitesimally rare."

New Jersey plans additional safeguards

"We will be looking at different possibilities of making our elections more secure going forward,"

New Jersey's Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) faced a major software glitch three years ago. Due to this glitch, thousands of non-citizens were wrongly registered to vote in the state. Now, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has announced that the glitch caused 6,600 non-citizens in the state to be mistakenly registered as voters between June 2023 and June 2024, and roughly 400 of them voted. State officials said all those affected had self-identified as non-citizens when they applied for a driver’s license or identification card but were added to the voter rolls due to the software glitch.According to a report by The New York Times, while announcing the findings, Sherrill said the registrations resulted from what she described as alinked to the MVC's voter registration system. The governor added that the affected individuals would be removed from the voter rolls. He said the state was working to protect them from possible legal or immigration-related consequences after they were registeredThe error was found and corrected in 2024 during the tenure of former Governor Phil Murphy, but it was not made public at the time, Sherrill said. Her administration officials learned of the matter last week and opened an investigation. The state has also hired an independent law firm to examine how the software failure occurred and said the findings of that review will be made public.Sherrill said the software vendor, Idemia, was responsible for releasing the faulty system and confirmed that the company was already being phased out in New Jersey. However, Idemia said the state's Division of Elections wasfor verifying voter eligibility after receiving information from the Motor Vehicle Commission.Sherrill said.Idemia, which says it provides technology services to more than 600 government agencies and has worked with New Jersey's MVC for four decades, is being replaced by Talus Software, according to Motor Vehicle Commission chief Rosalie Johnson.Around 400 ballots cast, state says no election outcome was affectedAccording to the governor, there isincluding the 2024 presidential election. If all 400 affected non-citizens voted in New Jersey's 2024 presidential election, they would account for about 0.009% of the state's total votes. Kamala Harris won New Jersey by more than 252,000 votes in that election. However, the New York Times report said it could not independently verify the figures released by the state.The disclosure comes as US President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers continue to push for the SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship for voter registration and place additional restrictions on mail voting. White House spokeswoman Abigail Jackson said,Joe Gruters, chairman of the Republican National Committee, also referred to the findings while urging Congress to pass the SAVE America Act. He said,David Becker, executive director of the nonpartisan Center for Election Innovation & Research, said administrative errors of this kind are uncommon and argued that state officials are best placed to resolve them.adding thatSherrill said New Jersey would continue its practice of not sharing personally identifying information of affected migrants with the federal government. She also said the New Jersey Innovation Authority is working to update electronic pin pads at MVC locations so voter registration information is displayed in five languages instead of only English.Sherrill said.In 2019, New Jersey passed legislation allowing undocumented immigrants to obtain driver’s licenses. Eligible residents can also register to vote when applying for or renewing driver’s licenses and non-driver identification cards at the Motor Vehicle Commission.
Article Summary: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has announced that 6,600 non-citizens in the state were mistakenly registered as voters between June 2023 and June 2024. State officials said all those affected had self-identified as non- citizens when they applied for a driver’s license or identification card but were added to the voter rolls due to the software glitch. The error was found and corrected in 2024 during the tenure of former Governor Phil Murphy, but it was not made public.

Article Title: Quote of the Day by Accenture CEO Julie Sweet: Have the confidence to focus on uncharted territory
Article Text:
Quote of the Day by Accenture CEO Julie Sweet

Quote of the day by Accenture CEO Julie Sweet



“Have the confidence to focus on uncharted territory. Take chances.”

What Julie Sweet's quote means



A message reflected in her work



The takeaway



Julie Sweet has built her reputation as the CEO of Accenture, one of the world's largest professional services companies with over 700,000 employees across more than 120 countries, on a leadership style that favours direct, actionable thinking over vague inspiration. This quote fits squarely within that pattern, and is essentially an instruction that says confidence comes first, followed by the uncharted territory. Chances follow only once the first two are in place.The quote works almost like a sequence rather than a single idea. Sweet does not say people should simply “take chances,” which is the version of this advice most commonly repeated and most easily ignored. She places confidence at the very start of the sentence, essentially as the precondition for everything that follows. Without it, uncharted territory remains just unexplored, avoided and left for someone else. Confidence, in Sweet's framing, enables a condition that has to exist before someone is willing to step toward the unfamiliar in the first place.The word “focus” is doing quieter but equally important work here.Sweet is describing deliberate attention directed at the parts of a business, a market or a career that remain unmapped. She says that the uncharted territory is a space that requires focus precisely because it lacks the existing frameworks, playbooks, or precedents that guide decision-making everywhere else.Only once confidence and focus are established does Sweet arrive at the final instruction: take chances. As per the executive, chances taken without confidence tend to be reactive, defensive or half-committed. Chances taken without focus tend to be scattered and difficult to sustain. Sweet's quote suggests that the quality of a chance is inseparable from the mental posture behind it.Sweet has repeatedly pointed to Accenture's own evolution as evidence of this principle in practice. The company has moved through multiple eras of technological disruption, which includes cloud computing, digital transformation, and now generative AI, and in each case, the businesses and leaders willing to move into unfamiliar territory ahead of certainty were the ones who ended up shaping the market rather than reacting to it.She has spoken publicly about the current AI moment in particular, describing it as a period where the biggest risk is not moving too fast into the unknown, but staying too long in familiar, well-understood territory while competitors experiment their way toward an advantage. Under her leadership, Accenture has pushed investment into emerging and unproven areas of AI application, often before client demand or industry consensus has fully caught up.That is a direct expression of the quote's logic: confidence precedes the willingness to explore, and the willingness to explore precedes the chances that eventually define competitive advantage.The quote applies differently depending on where someone sits. For someone early in their career, it is a reminder that caution can quietly close off the very opportunities that would otherwise define a career trajectory. For someone mid-career, it is a useful prompt to examine whether recent choices have genuinely stretched into new territory, or simply repeated safer, already-proven moves.
Article Summary: Julie Sweet is the CEO of Accenture, one of the world's largest professional services companies. Her quote is essentially an instruction that says confidence comes first, followed by the uncharted territory. Chances follow only once the first two are in place.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg: “Finding your purpose isn’t enough. The challenge for our generation is…”; a powerful lesson on building a better future
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Mark Zuckerberg



“Finding your purpose isn’t enough. The challenge for our generation is creating a world where everyone has a sense of purpose,”

Understanding the meaning of the quote



How a 2017 Harvard speech gave rise to the viral statement



A different way of thinking about purpose



About Mark Zuckerberg



Lessons to learn from the quote



Success is more than personal achievement: Career milestones and financial success matter, but true impact comes from helping others succeed as well.

Career milestones and financial success matter, but true impact comes from helping others succeed as well. Create opportunities for others: A meaningful life includes making it easier for more people to discover their own purpose.

A meaningful life includes making it easier for more people to discover their own purpose. Supportive communities matter: Schools, workplaces, families and communities play a vital role in helping people grow and contribute.

Schools, workplaces, families and communities play a vital role in helping people grow and contribute. Small actions can make a big difference: Mentoring, sharing knowledge, volunteering or offering guidance can positively shape someone else's future.

Mentoring, sharing knowledge, volunteering or offering guidance can positively shape someone else's future. Think beyond yourself: Lasting progress comes from focusing on collective well-being rather than individual success alone.

Lasting progress comes from focusing on collective well-being rather than individual success alone. Build systems that include everyone: Societies thrive when more people have equal access to opportunities and meaningful work.

Societies thrive when more people have equal access to opportunities and meaningful work. Purpose grows through contribution: Finding purpose is valuable, but helping others find theirs creates an even greater impact.

Finding purpose is valuable, but helping others find theirs creates an even greater impact. Leave a positive legacy: Real success is measured not only by what you achieve but also by the opportunities and inspiration you leave behind for others.

A common misunderstanding



Being successful can be defined as reaching personal milestones, either securing a dream job, having a career, or gaining financial freedom. However, could there be another way to define success beyond personal achievement? In one of his most popular quotes, Meta’s CEO Mark Zuckerberg gives us an alternative view on the matter. This quotation was first mentioned by him at the Harvard commencement address in 2017. It remains relevant since the statement changes the focus of the discourse from personal achievements to social contribution. It shows us that the fulfilment of personal purposes will become even more significant when it opens opportunities for other people to reach theirs, encouraging individuals to measure lasting success not only by what they accomplish, but also by the positive impact they leave on others. Know what is the meaning of Zuckerberg's quotation, its context, and valuable life lessons it carries.Initially, the quote seems to be about personal ambition; however, a further analysis reveals otherwise. The words at the beginning of the quote, "Finding your purpose isn't enough," refute the notion that one’s personal fulfillment must be his or her ultimate objective. On the contrary, the latter part redirects the focus toward the notion that only through the process of finding purpose for someone else can progress truly be made.In simpler terms, the quote implies that success of an individual becomes more meaningful when it helps provide chances for others.Mark Zuckerberg said this during the Harvard University commencement speech he delivered in 2017. In his speech, Mark Zuckerberg said that in the future the young people should learn to think not in terms of personal success but in terms of community, development, and society that gives many people a chance to feel engaged in something greater than themselves.Even though this sentence is often used separately, it was part of a much bigger discussion regarding equality, technologies, education, and other issues.Many popular quotes encourage people to search for their passion or follow their dreams. Those ideas focus almost entirely on the individual.This quote expands the conversation by asking what happens after someone finds direction. It suggests that purpose should not become a private achievement that ends with personal satisfaction. Instead, it introduces the idea that each generation shares responsibility for creating environments where others can also flourish.That perspective moves the discussion away from competition and towards opportunity. Purpose becomes something influenced by education, employment, social inclusion and community rather than determination alone.Mark Zuckerberg is an American tech entrepreneur who founded Facebook when he was a student at Harvard University. The company is now known as Meta Platforms Inc. and also operates Instagram and WhatsApp. Mark Zuckerberg’s career has always been marked by his constant references to connecting people via technology and promoting thinking about issues related to social responsibility into the future. These concepts were also the essence of his speech at Harvard University.This quotation is sometimes taken to mean that all people should have one purpose in life that would change the world. But such an interpretation would be wrong. Purpose does not need to involve world fame or outstanding achievement at all.It might consist of having a family, helping other people, teaching, running a company, doing arts, researching or working in one's community.The matter is not in how much a person contributes to the world but in providing the possibility for everybody to find something significant for him or her.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg said this during the Harvard University commencement speech he delivered in 2017. In his speech, he said that in the future the young people should learn to think not in terms of personal success but of community, development, and society that gives many people a chance to feel engaged in something greater than themselves.

Article Title: After raising prices, Apple will now let you 'rent' iPhones, iPads and Macs
Article Text:
FILE - The iPhone 17 Pro is displayed during an announcement of new products at Apple Park on Tuesday, Sept. 9, 2025, in Cupertino, Calif. (AP Photo/Godofredo A. Vásquez, File)

How Apple Upgrade works, and which devices don't qualify

Apple is preparing to launch Apple Upgrade, a lease-to-own program for most of its hardware lineup, on July 28 in the US. The service will cover most iPhone, Mac, iPad and Apple Watch models, and it works less like a payment plan and more like a car lease—you pay monthly, and at the end of the term you keep the device, hand it back, or roll into something newer. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman first reported the plan, with Klarna signing on as the financial backer.It doesn't take much to work out why now. Apple raised prices by hundreds of dollars across Macs, iPads and other devices last month, blaming an industry-wide memory shortage that the AI data-centre boom has made considerably worse. The iPhone escaped that round, but nobody expects it to escape September. Apple Upgrade lands right in that gap, and Apple reportedly plans to pitch it as the cheaper monthly option versus its existing financing.Lease terms run 24 months for iPhones and Apple Watches, and 36 months for Macs and iPads. Signing up requires a soft credit check. Paying off early, upgrading mid-term or keeping the device at the end are all on the table, though in some cases those moves come with an extra fee. AsThere are gaps. AppleCare is not bundled in, unlike the current iPhone Upgrade Program—a notable omission given AppleCare pricing has also crept up.Cheaper hardware is excluded too: the Apple Watch SE, the entry-level iPad, the iPhone 16 and the fast-selling MacBook Neo are all ineligible. Business and education purchases are out as well.Apple will stop taking new sign-ups for the iPhone Upgrade Program and standard financing to clear the runway. It's worth remembering Apple built and then killed its own in-house hardware subscription in 2024. Partnering with Klarna gets Apple the same customer lock-in without carrying the credit risk.
Article Summary: Apple will launch Apple Upgrade on July 28 in the US. Service will cover most iPhone, Mac, iPad and Apple Watch models. You pay monthly, and at the end of the term you keep the device, hand it back, or roll into something newer.

Article Title: AI data centers have promised to pay its electricity bills, but experts claim US households may still have to pay $23 billion more
Article Text:
Representative image

How AI data centers may push US households to pay more for electricity

Data centers may reduce some charges

Concerns over consumer representation

Major technology companies have pledged to cover the electricity costs associated with powering their AI data centers. Yet experts say US households could still end up paying higher electricity bills because of how utility costs are allocated. A recent report covering the PJM electricity market estimated that growing power demand from data centers is a primary reason behind $23 billion in customer price increases, which are expected to remain in effect until at least the end of 2028.According to a report by The Conversation, experts studying utility pricing have claimed that the issue is not whether data centers pay for their direct electricity use, but how the costs of expanding power infrastructure, such as substations, transmission lines and additional electricity generation, are shared among different customer groups. If those costs are spread across the broader electricity grid, residential customers could end up paying part of the bill.Electricity prices are set by state utility commissions, which determine how utilities recover the costs of new infrastructure and daily operations. While a data center is generally expected to pay for infrastructure built specifically to connect it to the grid, broader upgrades that benefit the electricity network are often shared among all customers.For example, if a utility needs to upgrade an electrical substation or secure additional power generation to support a new data center, those investments become part of the wider grid. As a result, regulators may allocate a portion of those costs to residential, commercial and industrial customers based on established pricing methods.Experts note that regulators examine thousands of utility cost items before determining how expenses should be divided among customer groups. The costs allocated to each group are then reflected in the electricity rates they pay.Another issue highlighted by experts involves a pricing method known as coincident peak demand, which measures electricity use during periods when the entire grid experiences its highest demand.Because AI data centers can rapidly increase or reduce electricity consumption using automated systems, they may be able to lower their power use during those peak periods. If they do so, they could reduce the share of costs assigned through this pricing method, even if they consume large amounts of electricity at other times.Experts point to cryptocurrency mining operations in Texas as an example where electricity usage has been adjusted around peak demand periods.Experts also argue that residential customers may have limited representation during utility rate-setting proceedings.Utilities, industrial customers, retailers and large data center operators often submit detailed proposals explaining how infrastructure costs should be allocated. Data center companies also have the resources to hire specialists in utility cost allocation.While most US states have consumer advocate offices that participate in regulatory proceedings, these agencies are generally required to represent the interests of all customer groups rather than argue for shifting costs from households to businesses. According to experts, this can leave residential consumers with fewer voices focused specifically on how infrastructure costs are divided.They also warn that if utilities build infrastructure for proposed data centers that are later cancelled, scaled back or become obsolete because of technological changes, those investments may still need to be recovered through electricity rates paid by other customers.Consumers should get involved in public hearings and provide comments during utility regulatory proceedings, experts say, because decisions on how to allocate costs can have a direct impact on future household electricity bills.
Article Summary: US households could still end up paying higher electricity bills because of how utility costs are allocated, experts say. Growing power demand from data centers is a primary reason behind $23 billion in customer price increases, which are expected to remain in effect until at least the end of 2028.

Article Title: Days after world’s biggest AI models repository Hugging Face announced that it has been hacked, OpenAI admits its AI Agents are behind the attack
Article Text:
Here’s what OpenAI said about the Hugging Face hacking incident

What happened during this incident

This incident occurred during an internal evaluation which prompts models to pursue advanced exploitation using complex attack paths, in an effort to quantify their cyber capabilities. We estimate maximal cyber capabilities by running this evaluation without production classifiers used to prevent models from pursuing high-risk cyber activity. Our benchmarks run in a highly isolated environment, with network access constrained to the ability to install packages through an internally hosted third-party software that acts as a proxy and cache for package registries.

The models identified and chained vulnerabilities across OpenAI’s research environment and Hugging Face’s production infrastructure to obtain test solutions directly from Hugging Face’s production database. All evidence suggests that the models were hyperfocused on finding a solution for ExploitGym, going to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal.

While operating in our sandboxed testing environment, our models spent a substantial amount of inference compute finding a way to obtain open Internet access, in pursuit of solving the evaluation problem. To gain access, the models identified and exploited a zero-day vulnerability (which we’ve now responsibly disclosed to the vendor) in the package registry cache proxy. With this access, our models performed a series of privilege escalation and lateral movement actions in our research testing environment until the models reached a node with Internet access.

After gaining Internet access, the models inferred that Hugging Face potentially hosted models, datasets and solutions for ExploitGym. Knowing this, the model searched for and successfully found ways to gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation. In one example, the model chained together multiple attack vectors, including using stolen credentials and zero-day vulnerabilities to find a remote code execution path on the Hugging Face servers. OpenAI’s security team discovered this anomalous activity internally.

Hugging Face’s security team and agents detected and stopped the activity on their infrastructure and had already begun containment and forensic reconstruction with their own open-source models when our teams connected. We are actively working with them to continue to investigate the incident. We are grateful for Hugging Face’s rapid and close collaboration on investigation and remediation.

Actions we are taking now

As part of the investigation, we are implementing strict controls in infrastructure configuration at the cost of research velocity while the vulnerabilities are patched. We are regularly briefing our Safety and Security Committee on these controls and their impact.

We’re working with Hugging Face to forensically investigate the incident.

We’ve responsibly disclosed the identified zero-day vulnerability in the internally-hosted third-party software and are working with them to patch.

We’ve brought Hugging Face into the trusted access⁠ program and are supporting their teams in rapidly using our models’ capabilities to improve their defenses.

We’re improving and adding stronger protections around future training and evaluations. This week, we published a blog on improving safety and alignment in an era of long horizon models⁠. These deployment safeguards were intentionally not enabled during this evaluation because it was aimed at testing cyber vulnerabilities. This incident points to the need to further strengthen our model’s alignment, cyber protections during evaluation time, and monitoring during internal testing.

Our approach to evaluating advanced cyber capabilities

As we recently⁠ shared, AI is accelerating the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities. The primary lesson from this incident is that model security and safety must keep pace with rapidly advancing capabilities. We are strengthening the containment, monitoring, access controls, and evaluation practices used during model development.

UK AISI’s evaluation shows that models such as GPT‑5.6 Sol are increasingly able to sustain complex, multi-step cyber operations over long time horizons. This incident implies these theoretical capabilities do apply in real-world settings.

Chart from the UK AI Security Institute comparing recent open-weight models and frontier models on long-horizon cyber ranges.

The incident also makes clear that advanced models can discover and exploit novel attack paths in real-world systems without source-code access. It highlights that advanced cyber capabilities must be developed alongside stronger safeguards and defensive tools.

We believe advanced cyber capable models need to help security teams find weaknesses before attackers do, understand how vulnerabilities can be chained, and remediate them at machine speed. We are using these capabilities to continue strengthening protections around infrastructure configuration and model evaluation environments; we will share our findings and best practices as we learn. We encourage other defenders to apply for trusted access⁠ and experiment with these models now to translate these capabilities into better prevention, faster detection, and more effective incident response.

Sam Altman-led OpenAI has admitted that its AI models were responsible for the hacking attempt that targeted AI platform Hugging Face last week. Sharing an official statement on the incident, the chatGPT-maker said that the incident took place during an internal test designed to measure advanced cyber capabilities. “Last week, Hugging Face disclosed a new kind of security incident after they detected and contained an AI agent that compromised their infrastructure, something we expect to become more commonplace with the proliferation of increasingly cyber-capable models,” OpenAI said. “After investigating, we now know that this particular incident was driven by a combination of OpenAI models — including GPT‑5.6 Sol and an even more capable pre-release model, all with reduced cyber refusals for evaluation purposes — while being internally tested on a benchmark⁠ of cyber capabilities,” the AI company added.According to OpenAI, the AI models found and exploited multiple vulnerabilities, gained internet access and attempted to retrieve data from Hugging Face's production systems. The company called it an "unprecedented cyber incident" and said it has since strengthened its safeguards while continuing its investigation with Hugging Face.“We consider this incident to be an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities, and are responding accordingly. We are sharing preliminary findings at this stage to help defenders understand what happened and to help calibrate on what models are now capable of. We will continue to conduct a thorough investigation alongside Hugging Face and will share more details on the vulnerabilities, incident, and findings when our investigation is complete,” the company stated.
Article Summary: OpenAI has admitted that its AI models were responsible for hacking platform Hugging Face. The incident occurred during an internal evaluation which prompts models to pursue advanced exploitation using complex attack paths. All evidence suggests that the models were hyperfocused on finding a solution for ExploitGym.

Article Title: Internet-famous eagle mom Jackie rescued after fight with other birds, Friends of Big Bear Valley post update: Jackie is a strong eagle and we as a community will...
Article Text:
Why officials took days to confirm it was Jackie

What's next for Jackie, Shadow and the fledglings

Jackie, the bald eagle mom watched by millions on the Big Bear Lake nest cam, is recovering at a California rehabilitation facility after being rescued near Dana Point Park. Wildlife experts picked up the injured adult eagle on July 17, days after she vanished from the livestream that has turned her family into a global obsession.The rescue followed a ground scuffle with two younger eagles. Cell phone footage showed the adult flipping onto her back and fighting off the pair with her talons, but she couldn't fly away — a detail that first tipped off viewers something was wrong. She's now stable and being treated at an unnamed specialty care facility while her mate Shadow holds down the nest.Confirming the bird's identity wasn't straightforward. Jackie isn't banded, and Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV) noted several visiting eagles have been circling the area lately. But after reviewing newly released photos from the rescue, the nonprofit now believes the injured eagle is their Jackie. She had been missing from the nest cameras for days, while Shadow and their two fledglings, Sandy and Luna, kept appearing on schedule.The Los Angeles County Department of Parks and Recreation, whose San Dimas Raptor Rescue team handled the pickup, urged patience. Officials said the eagle's identity and sex hadn't been formally verified and asked the public to lean on confirmed updates rather than speculation.What caused the injury remains unknown. Rival eagles sometimes move into occupied territory to push out resident pairs, and food theft mid-hunt is another possibility.FOBBV posted a Monday afternoon update after connecting with the rehab center. "Jackie is stable and they are waiting on diagnostic results that can take several days," the group wrote, adding that she's a strong eagle and the community will get through this together. There's no timeline yet for what recovery looks like.Meanwhile, Shadow has stepped up. FOBBV called him an excellent mate and father, feeding Sandy and Luna while guarding the nest and territory on his own. The two juveniles are close to fledging, which typically happens between 10 and 14 weeks of age.Jackie and Shadow first paired up in 2018 and have weathered plenty — lost eggs, a chick killed in a 2025 snowstorm, and a proposed housing development near their foraging grounds. Fans are now hoping for one more comeback. As one commenter put it on the county parks page: "You have a celebrity in your midst!"
Article Summary: Jackie, the bald eagle mom watched by millions on the Big Bear Lake nest cam, is recovering at a rehabilitation facility. Wildlife experts picked up the injured adult eagle on July 17, days after she vanished from the livestream. The rescue followed a ground scuffle with two younger eagles.

Article Text:
Larry Ellison

How and why Larry Elisson, Jeff Bezos and other billionaires are expanding their compounds



Larry Ellison and several other billionaires may be increasingly buying neighbouring homes and land to create larger private compounds. A report claims that the Oracle founder, hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin, Jack Daniel's heiress Dace Brown Stubbs and several other wealthy buyers are doing this. According to Coldwell Banker's midyear luxury market report, the trend has given rise to terms such as "Landmaxxing", which means acquiring additional land to expand a property, and "defensive buying," where buyers purchase adjacent land to preserve privacy or protect views.Citing the report, The Wall Street Journal noted that searches for US. luxury properties doubled in the first five months of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Searches for buildable land jumped 97% year-over-year, and searches for private islands and estates more than doubled, indicating rising demand for larger, multi-parcel properties.Among the buyers highlighted in the report is Citadel founder Ken Griffin, who has spent more than $450 million assembling a 27-acre compound in Palm Beach. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has purchased properties worth more than $230 million on Miami's Indian Creek Island, while Oracle founder Larry Ellison has continued acquiring neighbouring properties in Malibu, California, Incline Village, Nevada, and Manalapan, Florida.A real estate agent named Danny Hertzberg working for Coldwell Banker Realty said many buyers now see adjacent properties as both lifestyle assets and long-term investments."This is more sought-after than the 40,000-square-foot house. For some people, it is privacy and security. For others, it is a hedge against inflation,” he said.He added that neighbouring property owners are often the first buyers approached when a home goes on sale because they are willing to pay more to expand their holdings.Real estate agents say buyers are using neighbouring properties for a range of purposes, including guest accommodation, staff housing, gardens, boating facilities, gyms, spas and sports courts.Venture capitalist Benjamin Ling expanded his holdings on Miami Beach's Palm Island by purchasing the waterfront property next to his home. Investor Ibrahim Al-Rashid also bought two neighbouring homes on Hibiscus Island, later building a guesthouse with a gym, spa and a man-made fish pond alongside his primary residence.Businessman Patrick Dovigi purchased three nearby parcels last year, with plans to add a gym, spa and cabana next to his waterfront home, along with a padel court on another lot across the street.Some buyers are also engaging in what Hertzberg described as "defensive buying," purchasing adjacent land to create a buffer between themselves and future developments.Dace Brown Stubbs, whose family founded the company behind Jack Daniel's, said she expanded her Colorado ranch after concerns that new construction could alter the surrounding landscape."I hated the thought of a giant house or two being built on these beautiful fields,” she said.Stubbs initially purchased a 14.26-acre ranch and later spent an additional $1.15 million over several years to acquire another 40 acres to preserve the property's views.The report also highlighted WeatherTech founder David MacNeil, who has acquired multiple adjacent parcels in Manalapan, Florida. One nearby parcel is also being purchased by Larry Ellison, further expanding the Oracle founder's existing compound in the area.According to Coldwell Banker, average luxury single-family home sales volume increased 2.8% year over year between January and May, while the median luxury home price rose 4.7% to $1.83 million. The brokerage said the luxury market has continued to be driven largely by cash buyers and long-term wealth creation rather than mortgage rates.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison, Ken Griffin, Jeff Bezos and others are buying neighbouring homes and land to create larger private compounds. Article Text:

Birds and aquatic life found around floating solar farm

Bird sounds at farm suggest possible nesting under solar panels

A floating solar farm in the Netherlands may be doing more than just producing clean electricity. Scientists say they heard bird sounds coming from beneath the solar panels, a possibility that birds could be nesting under the structure. The finding comes from a study by researchers that looked at how floating solar farms affect local wildlife. As part of the study, researchers found that underwater shelters installed below the panels attracted hundreds of fish and thousands of small aquatic creatures over three years. The results suggest that, with the right design, floating solar farms could support biodiversity instead of harming local ecosystems.The research focused on the Bomhofsplas Solar Farm, a floating solar project built on a lake in the Netherlands. Between 2020 and 2023, researchers installed 20 underwater "Biohuts", cage-like structures beneath different parts of the solar farm, designed to provide shelter and food for small fish while helping scientists understand how floating solar farms affect aquatic ecosystems.By the end of the study, the Biohuts had attracted more than 400 fish and nearly 2,000 invertebrates, including mussels and sponges.Researchers said the structures gradually developed into small ecosystems that supported life higher up the food chain.The study also found signs that birds may be using the floating solar farm. In a 2021 paper published in the journal Sustainability, researchers reported hearing bird sounds beneath the solar panels, suggesting that nests could be present under the floating structures.Researchers believe the latest findings show that carefully designed floating solar farms could reduce some of those impacts while creating new habitats for wildlife.Besides supporting wildlife, floating solar panels also provide shade that can help reduce water evaporation. The water below also naturally cools the panels, which can improve their performance.
Article Summary: Bird sounds heard beneath floating solar farm in the Netherlands. Researchers found underwater shelters attracted hundreds of fish and thousands of small aquatic creatures over three years. Floating solar farms could support biodiversity instead of harming local ecosystems, say researchers. The structures gradually developed into small ecosystems that supported life higher up the food chain.

Article Title: Now, it’s AI cost control, and a move beyond LLMs
Article Text: Mumbai: The AI race is entering a more practical phase, where companies are asking how to control costs, secure data, and run AI systems at scale after the initial rush to experiment with large language models (LLMs), said Jonathan Bryce, executive director for cloud infrastructure at the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and the Linux Foundation.Bryce said the conversation around AI infrastructure has changed sharply over the past year. Earlier, he would often be asked how cloud-native technologies fit into an AI world. That question has faded, he said, as enterprises now understand that infrastructure is central to AI deployment.“People today understand that cloud is the substrate that’s powering all of the AI workloads,” Bryce told TOI on the sidelines of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon India in Mumbai.The bigger concern now is cost. Bryce compared the current AI cycle to the early cloud boom, when companies rushed to move workloads to the cloud and later began rethinking spend after receiving large bills.“Now it’s like, how do we stop runaway AI cost?” he said.He said enterprises are constrained by access to GPUs, power availability and the need to use expensive hardware more efficiently. Token consumption is also becoming harder to manage because AI usage is less predictable than traditional cloud workloads.Bryce said organisations are now trying to measure the business value of tokens, whether they are bought from companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic or produced on their own systems.Security and private data are also pushing enterprises to think more seriously about owning parts of their AI infrastructure. Bryce said frontier models already contain large amounts of publicly available information, but they do not contain a company’s proprietary data. That data, he said, could become a key source of competitive advantage.Bryce also said the industry may be looking too narrowly at LLMs. LLMs are largely suited to knowledge work, he said, while the next phase of AI could include computer vision, robotics, autonomous vehicles, agriculture, industrial systems and other real-world applications.“We’re still with AI in the equivalent of 1999-2000 on the Internet,” he said.India, Bryce said, is well placed for the next phase of cloud-native and AI infrastructure because of its young and highly technical developer base. He said the KubeCon audience in India skews younger than some other global editions and is deeply technical.CNCF is a non-profit subsidiary of the Linux Foundation. Established in 2015, CNCF serves as a vendor-neutral hub to host and nurture critical open-source infrastructure projects, most notably Kubernetes, Prometheus and Envoy.
Article Summary: Companies are asking how to control costs, secure data, and run AI systems at scale. Jonathan Bryce, executive director for cloud infrastructure at the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and the Linux Foundation, said the conversation around AI infrastructure has changed sharply over the past year.

Article Title: HDFC, Birla funds lead Ather’s Rs 1,300 crore QIP
Article Text: Bengaluru: HDFC Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund were the biggest buyers in Ather Energy’s Rs 1,300 crore institutional share sale, together picking up more than a quarter of the issue.Mutual funds dominated the fundraise. HDFC’s schemes took about 13.5% of the shares on offer, while Aditya Birla Sun Life funds bought another 13.1%. Ather is separately raising Rs 1,200 crore from existing investors Hero MotoCorp and the India-Japan Fund, as well as founders Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain.Together, the two deals will bring in about Rs 2,500 crore. The fresh capital will give Ather more room to spend on factories, new scooters and technology as competition intensifies in India’s electric two-wheeler market.The company is developing a new scooter platform aimed at a wider, more price-conscious customer base. It is also setting up a 98-acre factory in Maharashtra. The first phase is expected to add capacity for five lakh vehicles a year.Ather has been expanding after its stock-market listing last year. Its Rizta family scooter has helped lift sales, while its retail network has grown rapidly.The company currently trails TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto in electric two-wheeler registrations. Article Title: Pentagon hit by AI's 'biggest problem' after the whole Army reportedly burned through the whole year of tokens for just one service
Article Text:
The Pentagon

Army token pool runs empty



Reliability concerns amid rollouts



Just weeks after highlighting that nearly half of its 3.5 million military and civilian personnel have been using artificial intelligence (AI) on the job, the Department of War (formerly Department of Defense) has hit a massive computational wall. The US Army has reportedly burned through its entire annual budget of AI processing “tokens” in a matter of weeks, forcing military leaders to re-impose strict usage caps across departments, a report has said.According to Wired, the shortage highlights growing concern over corporate and governmental ‘overconsumption’ of generative AI tools even as other organisations struggle to manage skyrocketing cloud computing costs.In May 2026, the Army Chief Information Officer (CIO) announced that personnel would be granted virtually unlimited access to generative AI. However, internal emails sent to members of the Army’s Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) revealed a sharp reversal by mid-June.“Although the Army CIO announced in May 2026 that they were offering unlimited tokens, by mid-June the Army CIO pool was exhausted of tokens and had to re-establish limits.Apparently the whole Army burned through the whole year of tokens for just one service,” an Army insider told WIRED.The service in question is Ask Sage: a secure, accredited platform that allows military personnel to run top commercial AI models, including OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Alphabet’s Gemini and Meta’s Llama. The AI models are being used for tasks like rewriting job descriptions and processing procurement acquisitions.Previously, to encourage adoption, the Army initially granted workers at least 200,000 tokens per month and automatically bumped up allowances for heavy users. They even sent reminder emails to inactive employees urging them to use their allotments. That aggressive push led to rapid exhaustion of the Army's annual 100-million-token “enterprise pack.”Despite token depletion, the Pentagon continues to integrate AI into sensitive workflows, the report said, indicating that the DOW recently cut staff at the Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, opting instead to develop automated AI software to evaluate civilian casualty risks in active combat zones.However, rank-and-file personnel express skepticism about whether the current generation of AI tools is ready for prime-time military deployment.
Article Summary: The US Army has reportedly burned through its entire annual budget of AI processing ‘tokens’ in a matter of weeks. The shortage highlights growing concern over corporate and governmental ‘overconsumption’ of generative AI tools.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Peter Thiel: I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible
Article Text:
Peter Thiel's 2009 line—"I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible"—still defines his politics.

What Peter Thiel actually said

"I no longer believe that

freedom and democracy

are compatible."

What the Peter Thiel quote really means

The reasoning Peter Thiel used to get there

What made Peter Thiel want to escape politics, not win it

Why the Peter Thiel quote still gets shared today

Peter Thiel has backed some of the biggest names in tech and politics, but one line he wrote in 2009 still gets quoted more than almost anything else he has said. In an essay for the Cato Institute called "The Education of a Libertarian," the PayPal co-founder and early Facebook investor walked through two decades of political disappointment before arriving at a blunt conclusion. He had run a student newspaper at Stanford, fought campus speech codes, and watched sharp people around him quietly give up on free-market politics. By the time he sat down to write, he was ready to say the quiet part out loud—freedom and democracy, in his view, no longer fit together.Thiel isn't calling democracy a bad system. He's arguing it won't deliver the specific kind of freedom he values most. His reasoning: voters tend to choose bigger government, more spending, and more intervention—not the small-state, low-tax world libertarians want. So if individual liberty is your top priority, he suggests, the ballot box tends to work against you rather than for you.Thiel dates his pessimism precisely. He points to 1920 as the last decade an American could feel genuinely optimistic about politics, and blames the shift on the growth of the welfare state and the expansion of the electorate. That framing drew plenty of criticism at the time. Thiel later clarified he wasn't arguing to take anyone's vote away, writing it "would be absurd to suggest that women's votes will be taken away." What stayed was his broader doubt that voting could fix what he thought was broken.The essay's real punchline isn't the quote—it's what he proposed instead. If democracy couldn't produce freedom, Thiel argued, the answer was to build around it. He pointed to three frontiers—the internet, outer space, and seasteading, the idea of self-governing communities on the open ocean—as ways to "escape" politics rather than reform it. He framed it as a "deadly race between politics and technology," with human freedom as the prize.The line endures because it offers a rare, unfiltered look at how one of Silicon Valley's most influential figures thinks about democracy and power. Whether readers find it clarifying or troubling, it remains one of the sharpest statements of the tech-libertarian worldview—and a useful window into ideas that have only grown more relevant as tech leaders move closer to the center of public life.
Article Summary: Peter Thiel's 2009 essay "I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible" still gets quoted. The PayPal co-founder and early Facebook investor argued that democracy won't deliver the freedom he values most. He argued that if democracy couldn't produce freedom, the answer was to build around it.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Steve Jobs: "My job is not to be easy on people. My job is to…" - a powerful lesson on leadership, high standards and the difference between comfort and growth
Article Text:
Steve Jobs

Quote of the day by Steve Jobs

"My job is not to be easy on people. My job is to make them better"

What the quote actually reveals

Why he became known for this approach

The difference between demanding excellence and being destructive

Why honest feedback is often avoided

Other famous quotes by Steve Jobs

"Stay hungry, stay foolish."

"Innovation distinguishes between a leader and a follower."

"The only way to do great work is to love what you do."

"Quality is more important than quantity. One home run is much better than two doubles."

Why this quote is still relevant today

Most people prefer a leader who makes them feel comfortable. Steve Jobs argued that was never really the job. "My job is not to be easy on people. My job is to make them better," he said in a 2008 Fortune interview, before explaining what that actually meant in practice, "to pull things together from different parts of the company and clear the ways and get the resources for the key projects, and to take these great people we have and to push them and make them even better. " Most people only ever hear the first two sentences, which makes the line sound considerably harsher than the fuller explanation he actually gave right afterward.The version usually quoted stops after the first two sentences, but the rest matters. Jobs was not describing toughness for its own sake. He was describing a specific role, removing obstacles, securing resources, and pushing genuinely capable people toward more ambitious versions of what they were already doing. The demand was paired directly with active support, not simply criticism on its own.Jobs had a well-documented reputation for direct, sometimes uncomfortable honesty with colleagues. He described the trade-off himself. "I'm brutally honest, because the price of admission to being in the room with me is I get to tell you you're full of shit if you're full of shit, and you get to say to me I'm full of shit, and we have some rip-roaring fights," he said, adding that this dynamic kept weaker performers from settling into the organisation.He noted that people who survived that environment often described it afterward not as punishing, but as the best experience of their careers.This distinction genuinely matters. Pushing for better work targets the work itself, not the person doing it. Genuinely destructive behaviour attacks the person directly, offering no real path toward improvement. Jobs' own framing, pairing high standards with actively clearing a path for people to meet them, sits closer to the first category than the second.Plenty of organisations struggle specifically because difficult conversations get avoided entirely, a manager who suspects a project is weak but says nothing, a team that keeps using a process everyone privately knows is broken. Jobs' quote is a direct challenge to that avoidance, arguing that skipping every uncomfortable conversation rarely actually helps the people it is meant to protect.Modern workplaces often prioritise comfort and psychological safety, both genuinely valuable. Jobs' quote is a reminder that kindness and high expectations are not actually opposites. Believing someone is capable of considerably more than they currently think they are, and saying so honestly, can itself be a form of respect rather than its absence.
Article Summary: Steve Jobs: "My job is not to be easy on people. My job is to make them better" Jobs had a well-documented reputation for direct, sometimes uncomfortable honesty with colleagues. Jobs was not describing toughness for its own sake. He was describing a specific role, removing obstacles, securing resources.
